clue.text: Version that's current around northern neighbourhood

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters are placed on both sides of the next piece
something current is running or flowing, so the letters of the word before are set moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone describes a modern version of a guide to a northern district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's current' signals an anagram of VERSION, giving ENVIROS here, and 'around' puts the N of 'northern' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The surroundings or outskirts of a place are its local area, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Work on project usually slow at first

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Someone working on a project finds it usually starts slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical or literary composition is called by the Latin word for a piece of work.

clue.text: Church primate left? Part of it

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A question about whether a church's top cleric has departed, and whether he is a member of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primate' looks like an archbishop, which suits the church surface, but here it is an ape. 'it' in the definition points back to the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A small place of worship within a larger church or cathedral is one of its subsidiary sections.

clue.text: Catch contents of capsizing dust-cart? No chance

indicators.note: capsizing turns a vessel over, so the hidden letters are read backwards
the contents of a phrase are letters held inside it, running across the word breaks

explanation.surface: Someone doubts that anything can be retrieved from an overturned rubbish lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Catch contents' as the definition, but 'contents of' is the hidden-word signal, leaving 'Catch' alone as the definition. A dust-cart is a British rubbish lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch an illness is to contract it, as in picking up a cold.

clue.text: Taking out money with secret number -it has point

parts.note: withdrawing cash from an account is drawing it
a PIN is the personal identification number used at a cash machine

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws cash at a machine using their secret code.
explanation.walkthrough: A drawing pin is the British name for a thumbtack.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbtack has a sharp spike for pressing into a noticeboard.

clue.text: Stone arch initially has crumbled around left and right

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of the word arch
around says the scrambled letters go on both sides of the next piece
something crumbled has broken up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stone arch has fallen to pieces all around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbled' rearranges HAS to SHA, and 'around' puts L inside it to give SHLA.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressed, squared masonry blocks are a kind of building material cut from rock.

clue.text: Try to include tipsters' top selections in photo

indicators.note: to include says the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: to have a shot is to have a try
a nap is a racing tipster's most confident selection of the day

explanation.surface: A punter tries to get a picture of the best racing tips.
explanation.walkthrough: NAP, a British horse-racing term, is a tipster's strongest recommendation.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick informal picture taken with a camera is a casual photograph.

clue.text: What's the score?

parts.note: reads as asking about a match result or the situation, but a score is also an old word for a number

explanation.definitionFit: A score is an archaic term for a set of a dozen-plus-eight, so the question asks for that number.

clue.text: Charge devastated Hurons

indicators.note: devastated means wrecked, so the letters of the tribe's name are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An attack lays waste to a Native American people.
explanation.definitionFit: A forward rush or surge, as of attackers, is a charge.

clue.text: Fall to see young lady

definitions.meaning: to overlook something, not spot it
the title used for an unmarried girl or woman

explanation.surface: Someone does not notice a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both overlooking something and the form of address for an unmarried woman.

clue.text: Attractive result of Derbyshire custom, more or less

definitions.meaning: Derbyshire villages decorate springs with flower pictures, so the result is a lovely water source

explanation.surface: A charming outcome of a Peak District tradition, roughly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: Well dressing is a Derbyshire custom of decorating wells and springs with flower-petal pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase is a beautiful spring; as an idiom it means almost or to a fair extent.

clue.text: Spanish article on army accommodation

parts.note: a host is an archaic word for an army
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A piece of writing in Spanish about military lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' means the article comes after the army in an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheap lodging house for travellers or students offers beds for the night.

clue.text: Purchaser, allegedly, of a little ivory?

definitions.text: Purchaser, allegedly, of a little ivory?

parts.words: Purchaser, allegedly, of a little ivory?
parts.note: sounds like a dealer in elephant tusk, but the ivory is a child's lost milk tooth, bought for a coin under the pillow

explanation.definitionFit: The mythical figure who leaves money for a child's shed tooth is said to buy these small white objects.

clue.text: Those with stable businesses in footwear

definitions.meaning: people who run racing yards and prepare horses

explanation.surface: Secure firms in the shoe trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Racehorse handlers and soft sports shoes share the same name in British English.

clue.text: Wife's home-made soups — source of energy

indicators.note: home-made suggests something put together, so the letters are reassembled
source of asks for the first letter of energy

explanation.surface: A wife's homemade soups give a boost of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A wife is one example of a married partner.

clue.text: Excluded from the House, perhaps

parts.note: suggests being thrown out of Parliament, but the House is Christ Church, Oxford, whose students are expelled by the university

explanation.definitionFit: Being expelled from Oxford or Cambridge, such as from Christ Church, known as the House, is the British university term.

clue.text: Dull-witted boss engages detective

indicators.note: engages means takes on, so the first piece holds the second

parts.note: a stud is a raised knob or boss
PI is a private investigator

explanation.surface: A slow-thinking manager hires a private eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull-witted means lacking intelligence, which is foolish or dim.

clue.text: Significantly reduce time in which animals will be reared

indicators.note: in which says the next piece sits inside the time word

parts.note: a date is a point in time

indicators.note: reared means raised upright, so in a down answer the animals are written bottom to top

parts.note: mice are small animals

explanation.surface: A farm cuts back on the season for breeding livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be reared' turns MICE upside down to ECIM, which goes inside DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy a large proportion of something is to cut it drastically.

clue.text: Train for Winchester?

definitions.meaning: Winchester College is a famous English public ..., so the question mark marks an example

explanation.surface: A railway service to the Hampshire city.
explanation.definitionFit: To instruct is a verb sense; Winchester College is an instance of the noun sense.

clue.text: Working out, there's chance I'm fitter

indicators.note: working out means solving or rearranging, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone at the gym reckons they might get in better shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An engineer who assembles and repairs machinery is a skilled technician.

clue.text: Timid fellow's left getting a wigging

indicators.note: left says the piece has gone away

parts.note: timid means easily frightened, afraid
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A nervous man is given a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fellow's left' reads as 'fellow has left', so F leaves FEARFUL. A wigging is British slang for a scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: A long angry reprimand is a scolding, or a telling-off.

clue.text: Sprain remedy needed (injured in a car)

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone hurt in a car crash needs something for a sprain.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal cream from a mountain plant is used to treat bruises and sprains.

clue.text: Put on a ship, starts to use marine expressions

parts.note: SS is short for steamship

indicators.note: starts to asks for the first letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A sailor boards a vessel and begins talking in nautical jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on an air or manner is to adopt or take it on falsely.

clue.text: Juniors on commission?

parts.note: suggests junior salespeople earning a percentage, but the commission is a task given to young lads who run small jobs

explanation.definitionFit: Lads employed to deliver messages and run small tasks carry out commissions for others.

clue.text: Incline makes one walk laboriously, losing time

indicators.note: losing says a piece is dropped

parts.note: to tramp is to walk heavily

explanation.surface: A hill makes someone trudge, slowing them down.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloping surface joining two levels is an incline.

clue.text: Horse managed to get round ring

indicators.note: to get round says the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business
O looks like a ring

explanation.surface: A horse manages to circle a show ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse with a coat of mixed white and coloured hairs is so named.

clue.text: Wrinkle that's produced by endlessly stern look — without hesitation

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the trimmed look goes around the next piece
endlessly says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a frown is a stern look
ur is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A line on the face comes from constantly frowning, with no pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside: FROW goes around UR.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep line in the brow, like a groove in a ploughed field, is a crease.

clue.text: Reprimand business graduates coming in after time

indicators.note: coming in says the next piece enters the first

parts.note: late means after the expected time
MBAs are holders of a business degree

explanation.surface: A boss scolds business students who arrive late.
explanation.definitionFit: To criticise someone harshly is to scold or berate them.
